newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power slips on milder temps Friday.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power slips on milder temps Friday.

text.p: Forecasts of milder weather Friday in the Mid-Atlantic region pushed down day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, market sources said Thursday.
"It's not expected to be as cold tomorrow," said a PJM power trader.
Friday temperature in PJM would peak in the high 30 degree F range, about 4 to 6 degrees above normal with chance of snow overnight into early tomorrow.
Although PJM energy demand is expected to ease Friday, transmission capacity in the grid remains tight due to high power flows into the eastern part of the system.
The pool operator anticipates PJM would continue to run in a "split system" mode tomorrow, market sources said.
Peak, next-hour dispatch rates in the western part of the grid fell almost $1.00 to the $25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) level, while rates in the east held at $38.70.

Dispatch rates in the east are much higher because utilities have fired up expensive oil and natural gas plants to balance the grid, enabling them to bring in cheap, coal-fired generation from the west.
Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Friday (excluding transmission costs) fell to $26.50-27.00/MWh from Wednesday's $27.50-31.75 range for delivery today.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak delivery Friday held at $18.00-20.00, although PJM cost for next-day, off-peak generation was only about $15.50.
Next-week PJM deliveries dropped to $25.25-25.75 from Wednesday's quote of $26.75-27.25. PJM power deliveries for the remainder of February tumbled to $25.50-26.00 from $26.50-27.00 Wednesday.
March PJM power prices edged down to $23.80-24.00 from Wednesday's $23.85-24.05.
PJM prices for April and May widened to $21.80-22.00 from $21.80-21.90 Wednesday, while June PJM power tightened to $24.75-24.90 from Wednesday's $24.75-25.00.
July/August PJM power was actively traded, last quoted at $29.45-29.55, down from $29.70-$29.90 Wednesday.
PJM third-quarter deliveries remained at $27.55-27.75, and fourth-quarter PJM prices stepped down to $23.60-23.80 from Wednesday's $23.85-24.00.
Firm, peak 1998 PJM deliveries were last offered at $25.80 from a quote of $25.75-25.95 Wednesday.

Separately, swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate fell on forecasts of milder weather Friday and Saturday, quoted at $2.70-2.80 per million British thermal units, down 20-30 cents from Wednesday.
NYMEX Henry Hub gas futures extended yesterday's loss on long range outlook of mild weather across eastern U.S. At 1358 EST, the March contract was down 8.5 cents at $2.005/mmBtu.
